propositions: The gate matches config field names globally by bare attribute name, causing same-named fields on unrelated configs to satisfy the inert-field check even if never actually read, creating a false-negative class for commonly-reused names like enabled, path, timeout, remote, branch, mode.

Confirmed instance: CodeHealthConfig.enabled had zero read sites but passed the gate because UiConfig.enabled and other configs' .enabled fields put the bare name in a global set, while uniquely-named CodeHealthConfig.analyzers correctly tripped the gate.

The fix must resolve reads to their declaring dataclass owner rather than match bare attribute names globally, using six resolution routes: section-attribute names, annotations, local aliases, return types, branch unions, and cross-module call-site binding.

Four fields newly flagged by the corrected gate—McpConfig.readonly, McpConfig.allow_llm, McpConfig.allow_jira_sync, JiraConfig.allow_insecure—are all live and read through documented indirection (plumbing files or string keys) and receive factual read-via markers without product triage.

Test suite must include red-first proof that old gate silently passes inert field with reused name while new gate fires on it, and negative fixtures pinning that string-keyed reads via getattr and gate_enabled still pass.
Any read-via marker naming a closed rebar ticket id must be surfaced by the gate so expired markers do not persist silently.
